newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Talks on to free Western hostages on Nigeria barge.
newsitem.headline: Talks on to free Western hostages on Nigeria barge.

text.p: Negotiations have started to try to free 20 foreigners, 16 of them Frenchmen, held hostage on a cargo barge by Nigerian villagers, a spokesman for the company they work for said on Thursday.
Diplomats said the other foreigners were three Britons and one American.
They said they were being held on a cargo barge owned by French oil contracting firm ETPM by local people demanding employment. Earlier reports said they were held on a rig.
"It seems they want jobs but it is not very clear what the exact demands are," said one Western diplomat in Lagos.
She said negotiations were going between the French company and the villagers on the situation.
Ben Shibo, the spokesman for ETPM in Lagos declined to say why the foreigners had been taken hostage.
"This problem started yesterday morning and we are working hard to resolve it," said Shibo, adding "Everything should hopefully be under control by the end of the day, by the grace of God."
It is the second such hostage-taking by local people in the last few months.

Twenty-eight foreigners including 10 Filipinos and nine Frenchmen were held on a barge operated by ETPM about 30 miles offshore last Christmas by 60 Nigerian workers demanding higher wages. Apart from being deprived of food for two of the five days they were held captive, the hostages were not harmed.
"We have these kinds of problems all the time with local communities and it really is not as serious as it is taken," said Shibo.
In Paris a French foreign ministry spokesman said the French embassy in Lagos was in contact with both the local authorities and ETPM.
"We didn't get any information that the hostages are in bad shape so we think they are reasonably all right," the diplomat added.
They are held on the barge in the Escravos area near the coast of Warri in the oil-producing Delta state in midwestern Nigeria.
Chevron Corp's Nigerian joint venture is the biggest oil operator in Escravos, but a spokesman said the company was not involved.
